1. **The rule and the objection.** By the Pāṇinian rule "vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣavacane bahuvacanam" (विभाषितं विशेषवचने बहुवचनम् — *vibhāṣitaṃ viśeṣa-vacane bahuvacanam*, पा. ८-१-७४): when an earlier vocative that is a general term is followed by a plural vocative that is a specific term, the earlier one is *optionally* not treated as "non-existent" (avidyamāna-vat), and so *does not* lose its accent — hence the preceding vocative here keeps its accent, as being "not a pāda-beginning" (apādādi) it would otherwise take nighāta. **समत्सु (samatsu)** — The word "samatsu" is read among the forty-six words that signify battle, beginning with "raṇa" (Ni. 3-9 [as printed]). This word is always used in the locative plural only. Apart from this Ṛk it is found in Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-66-3; 1-70-6; 1-130-8; 1-173-7; [?]-12-3; 3-30-22; 4-20-1; 4-24-6; 4-38-4; 5-33-4; 6-18-6; 6-25-9 and others — in **29** Ṛks *(references re-read from the better scan; the first digit of the fifth falls at a line-break)*. **Skandasvāmī** explains this word as follows: "*ade bhakṣaṇe | sambhakṣayatsu parasparaṃ yodheṣu mahati yuddhe pravṛtte ity arthaḥ*" (अदे भक्षणे । संभक्षयत्सु परस्परं योधेषु महति युद्धे प्रवृत्ते इत्यर्थः — "'ad' is in the sense of eating; the meaning is 'when, in a great battle that has begun, the warriors devour one another'"). **p. 168 — the accent of "vṛṇvate" (concluded).** The page continues the argument of p. 167. The Bhāṣyakāra has said that there is a special application for this Ṛk. On the twenty-fourth day, at the morning pressing, the priest Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin is to recite, as the śastra-mantra, the two Ṛks beginning "ād aha svadhām anu" (that is, the 4th and 5th Ṛks of this sūkta [as printed]) and the one Ṛk "indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase" (the 7th of this sūkta) — a tṛca of these three Ṛks together; that tṛca bears the name "ṣaḷaha-stotriya." On this matter **Āśvalāyana** says in his Śrauta-sūtra, in the section "hotājaniṣva": "*indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase ādaha svadhām anv ity ekā dve ca*" (Āśv. Sū. 7-2). Though this sūkta has Indra as its deity, the Maruts are described in the six Ṛks of this sūkta beginning with "ādaha." For this very reason, the Anukramaṇī says "aindre maruta" (Anu. 2-22) — that in this Indra-sūkta there is a Marut-subject.  ==>  The Bhāṣyakāra has said that there is a special application for this Ṛk. **ग्रामादीनां च** (फि. सू. ३८ [as printed]; "2-15" on p. 227) — the "grāma"-class words are first-syllable acute, so "guhā" is first-syllable acute. **"Vahnibhiḥ"** — **वहिश्रिश्रुयुद्रुग्लाहात्वरिभ्यो निः** (उ. सू. ४-५१) after these roots the affix "ni," which is "nit" ("n"-marked), so from "vah" "vahni" is first-syllable acute (**ञित्यादिर्नित्यम्**). **"Avindaḥ"** — "vidḷ lābhe" (to obtain), a tudādi root; **तत्र (*tatra*)** — "in that"; the *tral* suffix after the seventh-case pronouns *tad*, *kim*, *sarva* etc. (Pā. 5-3-10, "saptamyās tral"); *tral* is *taddhita*, so the word is a *prātipadika*; the *sup* ending is dropped by *supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ* (Pā. 2-4-71); *d* → *a* by *tyadādīnām aḥ* (Pā. 6-2-102 [as printed]); *a* + *a* → pararūpa by *ato guṇe* (Pā. 6-1-97); *tral* is *l*-marked, so by *liti* (Pā. 6-1-193) the syllable before the suffix is udātta. **इन्द्र (*indra*)** — the second pāda's first syllable; since this is the beginning of the pāda, there is no lowering by *apādādau*; as a vocative it is initial-udātta by *āmantritasya ca* (Pā. 6-1-198). **राये (*rāye*)** — *rai* + the dative ending *e*; after the *ai*-ending word *rai*, the dative ending is udātta (*ūḍidam-pada-ādy-ap-pum-rai-dyubhyaḥ*, Pā. 6-1-171). **रभस्वतः (*rabhasvataḥ*)** — root *rabha rābhasye*; *asun* by *sarvadhātubhyo 'sun* (Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]) gives *rabhas*, initial-udātta as *nit*; *matup* after it by *tad asyāsty asminn iti matup* (Pā. 5-2-94), its *m* → *v* by *mādupadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ* (Pā. 8-2-9); the question of whether *rabhas* is a *pada* before *matup* (which would block *ruṭ* etc.) (by *svādiṣv asarvanāmasthāne*, Pā. 1-4-17) or has *bha* status (by *tasau matvarthe*, Pā. 1-4-19) is argued: *pada* status and *bha* status are both prescribed, and the source concludes by the maxim "ā kaḍārād ekā saṃjñā" (Pā. 1-4-1) that among the technical names prescribed from there up to *kaḍārāḥ karmadhāraye* (Pā. 2-2-38) only one applies, the later (*para*) one, *bha*; so *pada*-status is inapplicable and the rules (such as *ruṭv*-rules) that depend on it do not operate. **तुविद्युम्न (*tuvidyumna*)** — *tuvi* (much) + *dyumna* (wealth) as a bahuvrīhi; a vocative, initial-udātta by the vocative rule of the sixth adhyāya (no number printed). **यशस्वतः (*yaśasvataḥ*)** — "yaśo 'syāstīti yaśasvān": *matup*, with the *m* → *v* as in *rabhasvataḥ*; the long discussion (pp. 364–365) concerns whether the *vini* suffix of the sūtra "asmāyā-medhā-srajo viniḥ" (Pā. 5-2-121) blocks *matup* here — answered that, by the carried-over word "anyatarasyām" ("optionally"), *vini* is only optional — the "nityam" of *ekago-pūrvāṭ ṭhañ nityam* (Pā. 5-2-118) breaks the carrying-over, but it resumes in *tasau matvarthe* (Pā. 1-4-19), where the Mahābhāṣya gives the examples *yaśasvī / yaśasvān*; and by the Vedabhāṣya's general statement that *matup* has the sense of inclusion everywhere (*samuccaya*), and by Kaiyaṭa on the Mahābhāṣya on "keśād vo 'nyatarasyām" (Pā. 5-2-109; printed 5-3-109 on p. 365 [as printed]); *yaśas* is initial-udātta as a neuter noun not ending in *-isan* (Phiṭ-sūtra 26); *matup* is *pit*, hence unaccented; so the initial accent of *yaśas* stands. *(Sūtra numbers read from small print; pointers only.)*  ==>  **तत्र (*tatra*)** — "in that"; *ov* → *av* by "eco 'yavāyāvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-78); the nominative/accusative singular ending *am*/*su* dropped by "svamor napuṃsakāt" (Pā. 7-1-23); *ru*-and-visarga; initial-udātta. **बृहत् (*bṛhat*)** — stem accent. **विश्वायुः (*viśvāyuḥ*)** — a bahuvrīhi "viśvam āyur yasmin dhane"; initial-udātta by the suffix. **सहस्रसातमम् (*sahasrasātamam*)** — *sahasraṃ sanute dadāti iti sahasrasāḥ*; root *ṣaṇu dāne*; *ṣ* → *s* by "dhātvādeḥ ṣaḥ saḥ"; *viṭ* after *jana*, *sana*, *khana*, *krama*, *gam* in the Veda (Pā. 3-2-67); the *ā* substituted for the nasal (Pā. 6-4-41); the whole *viṭ* dropped; *sahasra* + *sā*; final-udātta by the root accent, and after compounding the second member's accent stands by "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139); *guṇa* by "sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-3-84) with *raparatva* by "uraṇ raparaḥ" (Pā. 1-1-51); all the letters of *vic* drop, giving *kar*; in the sense *karor bhāvaḥ* ("the doing"), *tva* by "tasya bhāvas tvatalau" (Pā. 5-1-119), giving *kartvam*. **अर्थम् (*artham*)** — root *ṛ gatau* with *than* ("uṣikuṣigārtibhyas than," printed "pā. sū. 2-161" [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives Uṇ. 2-12): an irregular formation with *thak*. **वृष्णिः (*vṛṣṇiḥ*)** — "sṛvṛṣibhyāṃ kit" (Uṇ. 4-486 [as printed]; the bhāṣya gives 4-49) after *sṛ* (to go) and *vṛṣu secane*, the suffix *ni*; **युक्ष्व (*yukṣva*)** — root *yujir yoge* ("to join"), ubhayapadī, with *loṭ* ātmanepada middle-second singular *thās*; *thās* → *se* by "thāsaḥ se" (Pā. 3-4-80); "savābhyāṃ vāmau" (Pā. 3-4-91) replaces *e* by *va*; *yuj* + *sva*; the vikaraṇa *śnam* is dropped by "bahulaṃ chandasi" (Pā. 2-4-73) — the source notes that this sūtra prescribes *luk* for *śap*, but in Ṛ. Saṃ. Aṣṭaka 1, Sūkta 9, mantra 1 (the word *matsi*) the Bhāṣyakāra gives the same *luk* for *śyan* by this sūtra, so the *luk* of *śnam* may be said here too, by the word *bahula*; *j* → *g* by "coḥ kuḥ" (Pā. 8-2-30), *g* → *k* by "khari ca" (Pā. 8-4-55), and *s* → *ṣ* by "ādeśapratyayayoḥ" (Pā. 8-3-59), giving *yukṣva*; the suffix accent stands, being taught later (*satiśiṣṭa*); in the Saṃhitā the final is lengthened by "dvyaco 'tastiṅaḥ" (Pā. 6-3-135). **केशिना (*keśinā*)** — "praśastāḥ keśā anayor santi": *ini* in the possessive sense by "ata iniṭhanau" (Pā. 5-2-115); the *a* of *keśa* dropped by "yasyeti ca" (6-4-148); suffix accent; the accusative dual ending *au* replaced by *ā* by "supāṃ suluk…" (Pā. 7-1-39). **वृषणा (*vṛṣaṇā*)** — root *pṛṣu, vṛṣu, mṛṣu secane*; *ā* dropped before *ka* by "āto lopa iṭi ca" (printed "6-2-139" [as printed], the number of the next sūtra; usually 6-4-64); final-udātta by "gatikārakopapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139); the dual ending as above. **अथ (*atha*)** — the particle is lengthened in the Saṃhitā (*athā*) by "nipātasya ca" (Pā. 6-3-136). **नः (*naḥ*)** — the rule "bahuvacanasya vasnasau" (Pā. 8-1-21) with the carried-over "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (Pā. 8-1-18): *nas* replaces the plural genitive of *asmad*, unaccented, since the word is not at the beginning of the pāda. **इन्द्र, सोमपाः (*indra, somapāḥ*)** — both are vocatives, wholly unaccented by "āmantritasya ca" (Pā. 8-1-19). **गिराम् (*girām*)** — "sāvekācas tṛtīyādir vibhaktiḥ" (Pā. 6-1-168) — the case-ending is udātta. **उप (*upa*)** — a *nipāta*, initial-udātta (Phiṭ-sūtra 80); with *śruti* it forms a *prādi*-compound ("kugatiprādayaḥ," Pā. 2-2-18); the rule "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) would give the second member's accent, but by "tādau ca niti kṛty atau" (6-2-50) — before a *kṛt* suffix beginning with *t* (other than *tu*) the preceding *gati* keeps its own accent — *upa* retains its natural accent. **चर (*cara*)** — wholly unaccented as a finite verb by "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28).  ==>  **युक्ष्व (*yukṣva*)** — root *yujir yoge* ("to join"), ubhayapadī, with *loṭ* ātmanepada middle-second singular *thās*; it is answered that by "numvisarjanīyaśarvyavāye 'pi" (Pā. 8-3-58) the intervention of *num*, *visarga* and *ś*, *ṣ*, *s* does not prevent the retroflexion, as the Mahābhāṣya says, "tatra śarvyavāye ity eva siddham"; the Vedabhāṣya's opinion that, because the intervention of the sibilant is "unobserved" in the Veda, the retroflexion arises, is discussed and is stated to be needless effort. "*Niṣ*" + "*ṣidh*": the *ṣ* is retained, and by "ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-41) the *s* of *nis* becomes *ṣ*, giving *niṣṣidh*; the compound with the genitive-dependent *puru* (*puru* is the object, "they bar many") gives *puruniṣṣidh* — a compound that, by "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139), keeps the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member. *Niṣṣidh* is a *kṛdanta* because *kvip* was added even though lost (by "pratyayalope pratyayalakṣaṇam"; *kvip* comes only after a root, under the heading "dhātoḥ," Pā. 3-1-91); the long argument that the compound is formed with a verb-noun that is not itself a *kṛdanta* by the usual "kṛd-grahaṇe gatikārakapūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" paribhāṣā (Paribhāṣā 28) settles that the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member stands. *nit* is carried over from "dhānye nit" (Uṇ. 1-9) and *uḥ* from "bhṛmṛśī…uḥ" (Uṇ. 1-7), so *u* comes after the ten roots *śvā* etc. and is *nit*; so *vasa nivāse* gives *vasu*, initial-udātta by "ñnityādir nityam" (Pā. 6-1-197). **दयमानः (*dayamānaḥ*)** — root *daya dāna-gati-rakṣaṇa-hiṃsā-dāneṣu*; **सुविवृतम् (*suvivṛtam*)** — root *vṛñ varaṇe* with *kta* in the passive; *vi* + *vṛta* are joined as *prādi*, and *su* with *vivṛta* as a further compound ("kugatiprādayaḥ," Pā. 2-2-18); since *vṛta* is a *kṛdanta*, the rule "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" (Pā. 6-2-139) would give the accent of the second member; this is set aside by "gatir anantaraḥ" (Pā. 6-2-49) (when a *kta*-ending word in the passive sense is the second member, a directly preceding *gati* keeps its own accent), so that the *vi* would be initial-udātta; this too is set aside by "parādiś chandasi bahulam" (Pā. 6-2-199), making the first vowel (*ṛ*) of *vṛta* udātta. **The long argument (pp. 417–418):** when *su* is then compounded with *vivṛta*, "gati-kāraka-upapadāt kṛt" would again keep the accent of the second member, and that *ṛ* stays udātta. But the objection arises: in *su-vivṛta* is *vivṛta* a *kṛdanta*? — the paribhāṣā "pratyaya-grahaṇe yasmāt sa vihitas tad-ādes tad-antasya grahaṇam" (Paribhāṣā 23) says that where a suffix is named, the item beginning with that to which it was added and ending in that suffix is meant; *vivṛta* is not *vṛta* alone — and the counter-paribhāṣā "kṛd-grahaṇe gati-kāraka-pūrvasyāpi grahaṇam" (Paribhāṣā 28) says that a *kṛdanta* includes one preceded by a *gati* or a *kāraka*; hence *vivṛta* is a *kṛdanta*. A further difficulty (pp. 418): the sūtra "gatir anantaraḥ" with "anantara" ("immediately preceding") appears to bar the rule when something intervenes, as in *su-vi-vṛtam* where *vi* intervenes between *su* and *vṛta*; "kte ca" (printed "5-2-45" [as printed], i.e. 6-2-45) being carried into "gatir anantaraḥ", the answer is that, because of the word "anantara", the paribhāṣā "kṛd-grahaṇe…" is not present in that sūtra, and the counter-example *abhyuddhṛtam* (where the intervening *abhi* does not keep its own accent) is cited to show the use of the word *anantara*; the discussion concludes (p. 418) that in *suvivṛtam* the *ṛ* remains udātta. *(The page ends with "so ends this great-sentence discussion.")* **सुनिरजम् (*sunirajam*)** — the root *aja gatikṣepaṇayoḥ* with the prefixes *su* and *nis*; "īṣad-duḥ-suṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal" (Pā. 3-3-126) gives *khal* after a root when *īṣat*, *duḥ* or *su* is the *upapada*, in senses of difficulty/ease; the argument whether *nis* intervening between *su* and *aja* prevents the *khal* is answered: the rule does not require that the *su* stand immediately before (cf. *suparihāram*, *duṣparihāram*); *khal* is *l*-marked, so the vowel before it (*a* of *aj*) is udātta by "liti"; with the *gati*-compound with *nis*, the accent of the *kṛdanta* second member (the root's *a* udātta) stands; compounding again with *su* gives the same by Paribhāṣā 28; the remaining syllables are lowered; the unaccented *a* of the suffix becomes *svarita* by "udāttād anudāttasya svaritaḥ" (no number printed). **त्वादातम् (*tvādātam*)** — root *daip śodhane* — the argument on pp. 419–420: by "ādeca upadeśe 'śiti" (Pā. 6-1-45) the *e* of the root becomes *ā* when a non-*śit* suffix follows; but the root is *daip* ending in *p*, with *ai*, which in the *upadeśa* is a diphthong-ending root? — the difficulty is resolved by the paribhāṣā "nānubandhakṛtam anejantatvam" (Paribhāṣā 6) that the diphthong-ending status of a root is not undone by a mere *it*-marker; *kta* in the passive by "niṣṭhā" (Pā. 3-2-102), giving *dā* + *ta*; the objection that *dā* + *ta* would then be *ghu*-class and so take *dad* in place of *dā* ("dādhā ghv adāp," Pā. 1-1-20; "do dad ghoḥ," Pā. 7-4-46) is answered, since *dāp lavane* and *daip śodhane* are specifically excluded and the substitute-from-*daip* *dā* is "lākṣaṇika," not *pratipadokta*; the paribhāṣā "lakṣaṇa-pratipadoktayoḥ pratipadoktasyaiva grahaṇam" is argued and disposed of by "gāmādāgrahaṇeṣv aviśeṣaḥ" (Paribhāṣā 106). *Tvā* — *yuṣmad* + *ṭā*, the third-case ending replaced by *ā* via *ḍā* ("supāṃ suluk…" Pā. 7-1-39); *tva* replaces the part up to *m* of *yuṣmad* ("tvamāv ekavacane," printed "8-2-97" [as printed], i.e. 7-2-97), *tva* + *ad* + *a*; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97); with *bha*-status the *ṭi* (*ad*) is dropped by "ṭeḥ" (Pā. 6-4-143), giving *tvā*; *yuṣmad* itself is from *yuṣ* with *madik* (Uṇ. 1-136); the *a* is udātta by "anudāttasya ca yatrodāttalopaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-161); the accent (pp. 420–421): the *ā* is udātta if a *prātipadika* accent applies; the third-case *tvā* compounds with the *kṛdanta* *dāta* by "kartṛkaraṇe kṛtā bahulam" (Pā. 2-1-32); the ending of the third-case word would be dropped by "supo dhātu-prātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71) but is not dropped by "tatpuruṣe kṛti bahulam" (Pā. 6-3-14); **नहि (*nahi*)** — by "saha supā" (Pā. 2-1-4), a *subanta* compounds with a capable *subanta*, so *nañ* compounds with *hi*; being a compound, final-udātta by "samāsasya" (Pā. 6-1-223). **त्वा (*tvā*)** — *yuṣmad* + accusative singular *am*; by "ṅe prathamayor am" (Pā. 7-1-28) the *am* is replaced by *am*, so that the ending counts as a substitute and "yo 'ci" (Pā. 7-2-89, the *y*-substitute before a vowel-initial ending not causing *ā* or *y*) does not apply; "tvamāv ekavacane" (Pā. 7-2-97) gives *tva* for the part up to *m*: *tva* + *ad* + *am*; "dvitīyāyāṃ ca" (Pā. 7-2-87) gives *ā* before the accusative; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), *savarṇa-dīrgha* by "akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-101), *pūrvarūpa* by "ami pūrvaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-107): *tvām*; then, under the headings "padasya", "padāt" and "anudāttaṃ sarvam apādādau" (8-1-18), "tvāmau dvitīyāyāḥ" (Pā. 8-1-23) gives the unaccented substitute *tvā* when not at the beginning of a pāda. **रोदसी (*rodasī*)** — root *rud* + *asun* ("sarvadhātubhyo 'sun," Uṇ. 4-628 [as printed]), *laghūpadha-guṇa*, *rodas*, initial-udātta since *nit*; the *u* of *asun* being *it*, *rodas* is *ugit*, so *ṅīp* in the feminine by "ugitaś ca" (Pā. 4-1-6); *ṅīp* is *pit*, so unaccented. **उभे (*ubhe*)** — *ubha* is final-udātta by the stem accent; *ṭāp* by "ajādyataṣ ṭāp" (printed "8-1-4" [as printed], i.e. 4-1-4), unaccented as *pit*; *ubha* + *ā* → *savarṇa-dīrgha*, udātta by "ekādeśa udāttenodāttaḥ"; before the nominative/accusative dual *au*, "auṅa āpaḥ" (Pā. 7-1-18) gives *śī*, the *ś* dropped as *it*: *ubhā* + *ī*, the *ī* unaccented as a *sup*; "ād guṇaḥ" (Pā. 6-1-87) gives *e*, udātta as a single substitute. **ऋघायमाणम् (*ṛghāyamāṇam*)** — "nṝn hanti" ["he slays men"] gives *ṛghā* in the nominative singular: with *nṝn* as *upapada*, *han* takes *vic* by "anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante" (Pā. 3-2-75); all of *vic* drops; as a *kṛdanta* it is a *prātipadika*; the *śas* is dropped by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ" (Pā. 2-4-71); the word "dṛśyante" in the sūtra serves to include other operations, so the *n* of *nṛ* is dropped and the *h* of *han* becomes *gh*: *ṛghan*. In the sense "becoming *ṛghā*, which one was not" (*abhūtatadbhāva*), *kyaṣ* by "lohitādiḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣ" (Pā. 3-1-13), the Lohitādi being an open (*ākṛti*) group; *k* and *ṣ* are *it*; with "lopaś ca halaḥ" carried from "bhṛśādibhyo bhuvy acver lopaś ca halaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-12), the final consonant is dropped; the *a* lengthened by "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (printed "7-8-35" [as printed], i.e. 7-4-25): *ṛghāya*; *laṭ*; by "vā kyaṣaḥ" (Pā. 1-3-90) the ātmanepada *śānac* ("laṭaḥ śatṛśānacau"); *śap*: *ṛghāya* + *a* + *āna*; *śap* is unaccented as *pit*, and the *śānac*, a *lasārvadhātuka* after the *adupadeśa* *śap*, is unaccented by "tāsyanudāttenṅidadupadeśāt" (Pā. 6-1-186); *kyaṣ* has the suffix accent; *pararūpa* by "ato guṇe" (Pā. 6-1-97), the single substitute udātta; *muk* by "āne muk" (Pā. 7-2-82), *n* → *ṇ*: *ṛghāyamāṇa*. *This derivation follows the Vṛttikāra; but in fact* kyaṣ *does not come here: the Lohitādi group contains only vowel-final words, and even as an open group* kyaṣ *does not come after a consonant-final word — the Mahābhāṣya on "lohitā…" says plainly "nāyaṃ halantād vidhīyate"; Kaiyaṭa, the Udyotakāra and the Kaumudī are cited in support, and the vārttika "lohitaḍājbhyaḥ kyaṣvacanam" with its rejection of the word ādi; there is also the Mahābhāṣya's separate denial for* n-*final words, "nāyaṃ nāntād vidhīyate". So the right derivation is: "ṛghā iva ācarati", with* kyaṅ *by "kartuḥ kyaṅ salopaś ca" (Pā. 3-1-11) after a subanta denoting the standard of comparison and the agent: *ṛghan* + *su* + *ya*; as a *sanādi* form it is a root by "sanādyantā dhātavaḥ" (Pā. 3-1-32), the *su* drops by "supo dhātuprātipadikayoḥ"; by "naḥ kye" (Pā. 1-4-15) the *n*-final stem is a *pada* before *kyac*/*kyaṅ*, so the *n* drops by "nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya" (Pā. 8-2-7); since "nalopaḥ supsvarasaṃjñātugvidhiṣu kṛti" (Pā. 8-2-2) makes the loss "unseen" only for those rules, it is not unseen for lengthening ("pūrvatrāsiddham," Pā. 8-2-1), and "akṛtsārvadhātukayoḥ" (Pā. 7-4-25) lengthens: *ṛghāya*; *kyaṅ* being *ṅit*, the ātmanepada by "anudāttaṅita ātmanepadam" (printed "1-3-1" [as printed], i.e. 1-3-12); the rest as above. **इन्वतः (*invataḥ*)** — root *ivi vyāptau*, *num* by "idito num dhātoḥ" (Pā. 7-1-58); *laṭ* third dual *tas*; *śap*; *ru* and visarga; *śap* unaccented as *pit*; by "tāsyanudāttenṅid…" (Pā. 6-1-186) the *lasārvadhātuka* after the *adupadeśa* is unaccented, so the root accent stands; "hi ca" (Pā. 8-1-34), with "aprātilomye" carried from "aṅgāprātilomye" (Pā. 8-1-33) — *aprātilomya* means favourableness — forbids the lowering of a verb joined with *hi*, so "tiṅṅ atiṅaḥ" (Pā. 8-1-28) does not apply. **जेषः (*jeṣaḥ*)** — root *ji jaye*; the augment being unaccented, only the root accent stands. **स्वर्वतीः (*svarvatīḥ*)** — "svaḥ āsām asti": *matup* by "tad asyāsty asminn iti matup" (Pā. 5-2-94); its *m* → *v* by "chandasīraḥ" (Pā. 8-2-15), *svar* ending in *r*, and also by "mādupadhāyāś ca mator vo 'yavādibhyaḥ" (Pā. 8-2-9), *svar* having *a* as penultimate: *svarvat*; **Kakṣīvantam, auśijaḥ**: the ṛṣi Kakṣīvān is the son born to the ṛṣi Dīrghatamas from a woman named Uśik. With *rarāvas* [as printed], if the genitive singular is added, the *saṃprasāraṇa* comes and the *vas* becomes *us*; so it is not *val*-initial. So, though the augment *iṭ* enjoined by *ārdhadhātukasyeḍ valādeḥ* is *antaraṅga*, there is a possibility that its condition, being *val*-initial, is destroyed by the *bahiraṅga* rule of *saṃprasāraṇa*. For that reason, by "akṛtavyūhāḥ pāṇinīyāḥ" (*paribhāṣā* 42) (if the destruction of the condition of an *antaraṅga* rule by a *bahiraṅga* rule is possible, the *antaraṅga* rule does not come first), some state the exclusion of the augment *iṭ*, that it does not come where *saṃprasāraṇa* comes. Others again, on the view of the *padāvadhika* explanation, that words are derived as having case-endings, if the word is analysed it is *rarāvas* + *as*. Now both the augment *iṭ* and the *saṃprasāraṇa* are due. Though the augment *iṭ* is *antaraṅga*, the *saṃprasāraṇa* is a rule enjoined by naming a particular word, so, being *pratipadokta*, it alone comes first. Then, since there is no *val*-initial *ārdhadhātuka*, the augment *iṭ* does not come: in this way they state the exclusion of the augment *iṭ*. Now, even without the augment *iṭ*, by "asaṃyogāl liṭ kit" (Pā. sū. "1-2-5" [?]) a non-*pit* *liṭ* not after a conjunct is *kit*; since the *ārdhadhātuka* *us*, which is *kit*, follows, the loss of *ā* comes by *āto lopa iṭi ca*. The *ṣ* and the rest as before. When *raruṣaḥ* is established in this way, if *nañ* is compounded with *na raruṣaḥ*, the form *araruṣaḥ* results. Now by "tatpuruṣe tulyārtha…" (Pā. sū. 6-2-2) the accent of the first member, an indeclinable, comes. The first member, *nañ*, is a particle, so it is initial udātta by "nipātā ādyudāttāḥ" (Pā. sū. "80" [as printed]). After compounding too this comes by the accent of the first member. So it need not be included in the *vṛṣa-ādi* group. The Vedabhāṣyakāra too has explained it in this same way at "gurudveṣo araruṣe dadhanti" (Tai. Brā. [no number printed]). Besides, in "yo no agne ararivān" (Ṛ. saṃ. 1-147-4) there is agreement of another mantra with this kind of explanation. So the derivation in this way is right for *araruṣa*. Yet here it is not taken in the way just stated; for in the Veda lengthening is not seen for *tarap* and *tamap*, while lengthening is seen for *gha*.
